polityNote: First-level units of the Republic of Moldova from the dissolution of the USSR (26 Dec 1991) to the eve of the entry into force of Law 37-XV (21 Mar 2003), which set up the raions of Law 764-XV/2001 for the 25 May 2003 elections; Law 764 Art. 21 kept the counties until the raions were formed, so the counties stood at least until then. Atoms: geoBoundaries MDA ADM1 (OCHA/UNHCR 2020, 37 units: the 32 raions of Law 764, Chișinău, Bălți and Bender municipalities, UTA Găgăuzia and the Transnistria unit; CC BY 3.0 IGO). Each unit drawn was matched locality by locality: the town and village lists of Law 306-XIII/1994 (raions 1995–98), Law 191-XIV/1998 (counties 1999–2003) and Law 764-XV/2001 (raions 2003) were parsed and compared; a unit is drawn only where its list equals that of the 2003 raion(s) on the same ground (and, before 1995, where the 1992 yearbook area equals the 2003 area). Result: of the 1995–98 raions only Briceni, Fălești, Șoldănești, Ungheni and Leova (Orhei and Telenești each differ by one village: Zahoreni came from Rezina, Cozești went to Sîngerei), and of the 1999–2003 counties only Cahul, Taraclia and UTA Găgăuzia, are unions of today's atoms; the other counties were assembled from communes and cut across the raions (unresolved, with the moved villages named). Transnistria (left bank) is outside Moldovan administration for the whole scope, Bender since the battle of 19–21 June 1992. The Căușeni atom includes right-bank villages under PMR administration (Chițcani, Gîsca, Cremenciug) and the Dubăsari atom left-bank communes under Moldovan administration (Cocieri, Molovata Nouă, Corjova); both are unresolved throughout. Check ① (2026-10-06): geodesic atom areas against published areas — Briceni 814.4 vs 814 (1992) / 814.44 (2010) km²; Fălești 1,071.4 vs 1,073 / 1,072.60; Șoldănești 595.1 vs 598 / 598.37; Ungheni 1,081.4 vs 1,082.62; Leova 764.3 vs 764.73; Găgăuzia 1,842.9 vs 1,848.5; Cahul county 2,408.4 vs 2,413.14 (Cahul + Cantemir, 2010); Taraclia 670.2 vs 673.69 — all within 0.6%.
